scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Tango originated in the early 20th century in Buenos Aires, with men dancing with men in brothels and on street corners.
After being popularized as a male-female dance in Paris, the same-sex origins were suppressed.
The modern Queer Tango movement was founded in 2001 in Hamburg, Germany, by Marga Nagel and Ute Walter.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Queer Tango serves as a space for LGBTQIA+ individuals and heterosexual dancers to explore gender fluidity and dismantle heteronormative codes.
It is practiced in milongas and at international festivals.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is improvisational, based on the 'marcar y responder' (signaling and responding) technique.
Dancers exchange roles (leader/follower) regardless of gender.
Specific movements include 'ocho' (figure-eight footwork), 'boleo' (leg flick), 'parada' (stop), 'sacada' (displacement of partner's leg), and 'barrida' (foot sweep).
Watch for Ocho, Boleo, Parada.

Formation: Couple dance, improvisational.
